sentences.text: Acantholipan was a herbivorous nodosaurid dinosaur belonging to the family Nodosauridae and the subfamily Nodosaurinae. It is the sister taxon to Nodosaurus, sharing a close evolutionary relationship within this group of armored reptiles.

This dinosaur possessed tall, spine-shaped osteoderms located above the hips, which served as part of its defensive armor. It is distinguished from other nodosaurids by a prominent, tapered ulna and a conical lateral thoracic osteoderm with an oval longitudinal section.
Acantholipan holds the distinction of being the first ankylosaurian species formally named from Mexico.
Its unique spine-shaped osteoderms above the hips set it apart from other armored dinosaurs known from the region.

A partial skeleton was first described in 2011 from fossils found at Los Primos near San Miguel in Coahuila, Mexico. The type species Acantholipan gonzalezi was formally named by Rivera-Sylva and colleagues in 2018. The specific name gonzalezi honors Mexican paleontologist Arturo Homero González-González, who chaired the Museo del Desierto.

The holotype specimen CPC 272 was found in a marine layer of the Pen Formation alongside another nodosaur and dates to the Santonian. This specimen consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull, including vertebrae, a rib fragment, limb bones, and a spike-like osteoderm likely from the posterior thorax.

Acantholipan lived during the Santonian stage of the Late Cretaceous, approximately 83 million years ago, in what is now North America. Fossils of Acantholipan were found in marine strata of the Pen Formation in Coahuila, Mexico, and consist only of postcranial material. The time range for Acantholipan is recorded as the Campanian, spanning from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
